items.title: Split Rating / Chunk Play (ADG 11.24.2026) and Recap
items.position: 'As the AI boom goes, so goes the broader US economy': PIMCO's Ivascyn says AI capex and disruption have made the finance/real-economy link much stronger, 10-year yields sit near post-GFC highs of ~5% and PIMCO is happy in quality bonds; PIMCO's Karoui finds the BBB-over-AA premium at 50bp (narrowest since 2002) while CCC-over-BB is 400bp (2020/2016/GFC levels) - IG tightness reflects hyperscaler releveraging and heavy supply, HY dispersion reflects fundamental stress. Grant's frames this as a case for trimming risk. Chunk Play: SF median home price $2.39M, up ~70% since start of 2025 on AI wealth. Recap: S&P -0.5%, Nasdaq 100 -2%.

numbers.claim: BBB-AA spread 50bp, narrowest since 2002; CCC-BB 400bp (PIMCO/Karoui)
10-year ~5% (Ivascyn)
SF median home price $2.39M, +~70% since Jan 2025

items.title: Hum Dinger (ADG 11.25.2026) and Recap
items.position: A BlackRock-led consortium is weighing a lower bid for Stack Infrastructure's Asia-Pacific data centers (smaller equity component, deferred payments, delivery contingencies - Bloomberg), which Grant's reads as ill for Blackstone Digital Infrastructure Trust: BXDC deployed $1.9B of IPO proceeds at a 7% cap rate with a 2.75% escalator in tertiary markets at ~50% LTV, is down ~25% since the Aug 28 bear case and trades at 0.8x NAV; MoffettNathanson calls a NAV discount 'potentially existential' for equity-funded growth. Recap: Nasdaq 100 briefly 20% below its early-October high intraday, S&P flat; 2-year 4.61%, 30-year 5.24%; WTI $84; gold $3,571; VIX 28 after topping 34.

items.name: Torsten Slok (Apollo Daily Spark): software credit faces a double whammy of AI disruption and higher-for-longer rates, with loan yields above 13% and a 2028-29 maturity wall.
items.title: The Distress in Software Is About To Get Worse
items.position: Software loan yields have risen above 13% and software equities have sold off as AI disruption and higher rates hit together; 2021-22 seven-year term loans with minimal amortization mature in 2028-29, and software was over 30% of buyout deal value at the peak.

numbers.claim: software loan yields >13%
maturity wall 2028-29
software >30% of buyout value at peak

items.name: Ed Zitron (Where's Your Ed At): Huang's reinstatement is a sign of fragility, not a fix - the industry is 'functionally in default' with ~$700B of backstops and vendor financing, ~$200B of GPUs in warehouses and OpenAI losing $10.9B on $10B of Q3 revenue.
items.title: Defective Accelerationism
items.position: The debt, circular financing and ROI gap remain after the CEO reversal; NVIDIA has put >$100B into AI across 293 deals since 2023 (WSJ), backstops and vendor financing total just under $700B (FT), Jefferies sees $44-62B of FY2028 NVIDIA revenue at risk, and an ING $500M data-center loan auction drew muted bids.

items.position: Of 12 prior occurrences, 11 saw NDX lower three days later (avg -5.4%, median -5.46%); all 12 had at least a -4.6% drawdown over the next 30 trading days, 10 of 12 at least -9.4%, with average and median 30-day drawdowns of -16%; average 30-day draw-ups ~10%, mostly after T+15.

items.name: Paul Kedrosky: the memory cycle is turning about six months sooner than forecast - NAND spot prices have corrected more than 20% and contract prices are expected to fall from Q1 2027 as Chinese demand destruction exceeds incremental North American demand.
items.title: Plain English Appearance, Memory Prices, Jobs Data, RSI, etc.
items.position: Memory forecasters are cutting AI memory outlooks; the turning point moved up roughly six months from a July forecast of H2 2027; NAND industry capex is still forecast +26.7% in 2027. Separately, research on 34.8M US job postings finds firms more exposed to agentic AI cut hiring growth over six months.

numbers.claim: NAND spot -20%+; contract decline from Q1 2027; turn pulled forward ~6 months
NAND capex +26.7% 2027

items.name: Mohamed El-Erian (CNBC, via Stocktwits): expects a quarter-point 'dovish hike' on Dec 9 that trims January/March hike pricing; sees margin calls and forced selling ahead with pressure spreading into credit via rising tech CDS, and is buying the tech dip 'very slowly'.
items.source: Stocktwits (Prabhjote Gill) write-up of CNBC interview
items.title: Mohamed El-Erian Is Buying The Tech Dip 'Very Slowly,' Says Nvidia Is 'Too Big to Wobble'
items.position: The Nvidia 31% pop was excessive and the investigations are unresolved; Nvidia's circular financing is the key investor question with effects on AI investment and growth; the whole sector faces more oversight; the US government holds direct stakes in more than 30 companies. CME FedWatch priced a 25bp December hike at 97.4% (Nocta, Nov 25 morning).
